translation_notes: initNs-only case (no initBindings anywhere in this test method): `initNs={"ex": "http://example.com/"}` is a static IRI known at transpile time, so it becomes a module-level `@prefix ex: <http://example.com/> .`, and the query's prologue is inherited from it, per the stratum's correspondence rule. No interpolation is needed.

`g.query(TEXT, initNs=...)` collapses into an `s{ }` island written literally at the point of use. `SELECT (ex:foo AS ?s) WHERE {}` returns a lazy `PreparedQuery` when called on a graph (`s{ }(g)`); the region calls `.serialize()` on the result, which `PreparedQuery` does not proxy, so `.execute()` is needed to obtain rdflib's actual `Result` object -- verified directly against ldpy/runtime.py's `PreparedQuery`: iterating or testing an island's truth value is enough for SELECT/ASK/CONSTRUCT, but getting the `Result` itself (to call a method on it) needs the explicit `.execute()`.

the region's WHERE clause is empty (`WHERE {}`): an empty basic graph pattern matches exactly once, unconditionally, independent of any triple in `g`. The stratum's usual fixture requirement (several solutions / zero solutions / non-matching neighbourhood) does not apply -- there is no graph data this query reads at all. fixture.ttl documents this rather than fabricating triples the query would never look at; see driver.py.

`self` (the test's own `self.assertEqual`) is not a graph, so the default `fixture=` wiring does not fit; `calls=` supplies a plain `unittest.TestCase('assertEqual')` instead -- `SparqlTestCase(unittest.TestCase)` in the source file defines no setUp of its own. The region's `self.assertEqual(...)` against the hard-coded expected JSON (copied verbatim into both original.py and translated.ldpy) is itself the oracle: a mismatch on either side already raises inside the call and fails the check.

Registration is via the package's setuptools entry points (rdf.plugins.store), not an import side effect, so no shim import is needed on either side.
